items.title: All Saints' Anglican Church
notes: Rev. Marty Levesque, Priest in Charge, All Saints' Anglican Church, requested that Council provide a grant of $120,000 from the Council Community Priority Contingency Reserve to fund the construction a new community centre at the All Saints’ Anglican Church at 400 Northfield Drive West.

Rev. Levesque noted that the current model of providing City-funded community spaces provides service gaps in locally accessible spaces. Rev. Levesque noted that the Lakeshore area has a high proportion of the population that is low income and/or comprised of visible minorities and that outcomes improve when community members lead the development of programming.

Jane Mitchell, President, Lakeshore South Neighbourhood Association, informed Council that the cost of renting space and transit time are barriers for the public to book rooms at centralized community centres such as the Waterloo Memorial Recreation Complex or RIM Park.
Rev. Levesque responded to questions from Council.
Mark Dykstra, Jim Bowman and Sanjay Govindaraj also responded to questions from Council.

motions.text: 1. That Council approve report CORP2023-029. 2. That as part of report CORP2023-029 Council acknowledges the actual 2022 COVID tax base deficit of approximately $1.5M, largely driven by reduced recreation revenue due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, and the COVID-19 related Enterprise deficit of approximately $0.5M, for a total 2022 COVID deficit of $2.0M. 3. That as part of report CORP2023-029 Council acknowledges the $1.7M in Federal / Provincial grant funds available for use in 2022, and directs staff to offset the 2022 COVID tax base deficit in full and partially offset the Enterprise deficits with these available grant funds. 4. That as part of report CORP2023-029 Council acknowledges the remaining 2022 non-COVID tax base surplus of $878,790. 5. That Council approve a $500,000 transfer to the Winter Control Reserve to return this reserve to its minimum balance. 6. That Council approve the remaining 2022 year-end non-COVID surplus of $378,790 to be allocated to the following reserves as per the Surplus Allocation Policy (Appendix A): 1) RIM Park Investment Reserve $200,000 2) $89,395 to the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve 3) $89,395 to the Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve 7. That Council approve that any adjustments as a result of the year- end audit to the final surplus figure be transferred to the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve (50%) and Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve (50%) in compliance with the Surplus Allocation Policy.
motions.text_html:
1. That Council approve report CORP2023-029.

2. That as part of report CORP2023-029 Council acknowledges the actual 2022 COVID tax base deficit of approximately $1.5M, largely driven by reduced recreation revenue due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic, and the COVID-19 related Enterprise deficit of approximately $0.5M, for a total 2022 COVID deficit of $2.0M.

3. That as part of report CORP2023-029 Council acknowledges the $1.7M in Federal / Provincial grant funds available for use in 2022, and directs staff to offset the 2022 COVID tax base deficit in full and partially offset the Enterprise deficits with these available grant funds.

4. That as part of report CORP2023-029 Council acknowledges the remaining 2022 non-COVID tax base surplus of $878,790.

5. That Council approve a $500,000 transfer to the Winter Control Reserve to return this reserve to its minimum balance.

6. That Council approve the remaining 2022 year-end non-COVID surplus of $378,790 to be allocated to the following reserves as per the Surplus Allocation Policy (Appendix A): 1) RIM Park Investment Reserve $200,000 2) $89,395 to the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve 3) $89,395 to the Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve

7. That Council approve that any adjustments as a result of the year- end audit to the final surplus figure be transferred to the Tax Rate Stabilization Reserve (50%) and Capital Infrastructure Reinvestment Reserve (50%) in compliance with the Surplus Allocation Policy.
